The "bad" cholesterol is low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and the "good" cholesterol is high-density lipoprotein (HDL). LDL contributes to plaque buildup in arteries, increasing cardiovascular risk, while HDL helps remove excess cholesterol from the bloodstream [American Heart Association, 2023]. 

For further clarification, the National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) also identifies LDL as the primary target for lipid-lowering therapies due to its role in atherosclerosis [NCEP, 2020]. 

Always consult a healthcare provider for personalized guidance.
